c.sl: One field since 2001 — the TSP® voltage sag compensator
c.ft: WESCO Co., Ltd. · Anyang HQ · Icheon EMS Plant
d1.p: What a voltage sag is, why it is fatal to a production line, and how TSP® handles it within 2ms — the company and the product in one flow.
p4.intro: A specialist manufacturer that has worked one field for 25 years — the TSP® voltage sag compensator. The only company in Korea that designs and builds the full lineup in-house, from single-phase 0.5kVA to three-phase 2,400kVA.
p4.v2: Power quality equipment manufacturing · voltage sag compensator (TSP®) specialist
p4.v3: HQ & R&D Center: Anyang, Gyeonggi / EMS Plant: Icheon, Gyeonggi
p4.v4: Semiconductor · Display · Automotive · EV Battery · Public infrastructure
p4.v5: Supplied to 15+ countries · $10M Export Tower Award (2018)
p4.band: 25 years · one field · Korea's only full lineup, built in-house
p5.lead: A voltage sag is a drop below 90% of nominal voltage lasting 0.01 to 1 second. It is not an outage, so it never appears in utility statistics — but precision equipment stops in that instant.
p5.li1: Equipment stops → hours to days of restart, cleaning and re-qualification
p5.li2: Wafers, panels and cells in process are mostly scrapped
p5.li3: No trip record remains, so the cause is identified late
p5.li4: Capacity and cost limit UPS coverage to a few critical tools
p5.note: ※ 70% originates outside the plant. Since it cannot be stopped on site, compensation in front of the equipment is the only remedy.
p5.band: Not an outage, so not in the statistics — yet it stops the line more often than one
p6.h: Before · After — What Happens on the Line
p6.lead: The same sag hits both lines. On the line with TSP®, it ends not as an incident but as a single line in a log.
p6.b2: PLC, servo and inverter trip on undervoltage
p6.b5: WIP scrapped · delivery delayed · cause unknown
p6.a2: Switches to INVERTER + EDLC within 2ms · 100% compensation
p6.a3: Equipment never notices and keeps running
p6.a4: Event logged automatically → time, voltage and duration report
p6.band: The line that used to stop now compensates and logs — a sag becomes data, not an incident
p7.lead: In normal operation power flows through the bypass at 98% efficiency. The instant a sag is detected, the inverter draws on EDLC (supercapacitor) energy and supplies rated voltage to the equipment.
p7.svgnote: Normal: BYPASS at 98% efficiency  ·  Sag: INVERTER + EDLC
p7.li1: No battery — no replacement, no disposal, no fire risk
p7.li2: No cooling fan — no noise, no dust intake, no fan failure
p7.li3: Installed beside the equipment — added line by line, no electrical room work
p7.li4: Compensation logged automatically — when and how much, kept as data
p7.band: Invisible at 98% every day, 2ms at the critical moment — the two faces of compensation
p8.lead: A UPS is built for outages; TSP® is built for voltage sags alone. Different targets mean a different cost structure.
p8.p1s: EDLC capacitors · no replacement for 10+ years
p8.p2s: Bypass in normal operation → minimal power loss
p8.p3s: Noise, dust and fan failure eliminated at the source
p8.p4s: Deployed line by line, no electrical room retrofit
p8.p5s: No lead-acid battery disposal · lower power losses
p8.note: ※ Cost and schedule are quotation examples for a FAB of the same scale. Actual figures vary with site conditions.
p8.band: Same line, one-ninth the cost — for sags, equipment built for sags

p9.t3: Three-phase · high capacity · whole line, incoming feeder
p9.ad: One beside each critical tool. Easy to expand in stages, with no electrical room work.
p9.bd: One high-capacity unit at the distribution board or MCC. Best for new lines and FABs.
p9.band: Single-phase 0.5kVA to three-phase 2,400kVA — designed and built in-house
p10.lead: Every sag TSP® compensates is logged with its time, voltage and duration. For the first time, “how many sags hit our plant” has a number for an answer.
p10.ft: ※ Example screen — the live view shows data from your own site

p10.band: Compensation is the baseline, the record is the asset — sag history justifies the investment

d2.p: Semiconductor, display, automotive, EV battery, public infrastructure — each industry loses different equipment to a sag and protects it differently. Here is where and how TSP® is applied in each.
p13.band: 25 years proven by global top-tier manufacturers
p14.risk: A 0.1-second dip breaks the vacuum, temperature and gas sequence, and every wafer in process is scrapped. Restart, cleaning and re-qualification take hours — 20 events a year at a 154kV FAB, 520M KRW each.
p14.h1: Distributed per tool to SEMI F47 (A) — beside the tool, per vendor spec
p14.h2: New FABs combine high-capacity units at the MCC (B)
p14.h3: Sag-VIEWER consolidates FAB-wide events on one screen
p14.band: SEMI F47 compliant · protection tool by tool — the standard FAB configuration
p15.risk: With large glass substrates, one stop of a transfer robot or deposition chamber leads to breakage and contamination — and OLED deposition needs the chamber stabilized again before it can resume.
p15.h1: Distributed installation (A) centred on deposition and transfer tools
p15.h2: New lines in Korea and China add line-level high-capacity units (B)
p15.h3: Overseas sites are installed and serviced through the local support network
p15.band: Korea's two major panel makers and leading Chinese makers — local support on overseas lines
p16.risk: In body and paint shops where hundreds of robots run in sync, one trip stops them all. On a paint line, bodies in process must be repainted or scrapped once work restarts.
p16.h1: Distributed installation (A) at robot control panels and PLCs
p16.h2: Three-phase high-capacity units (B) for paint lines, conveyors and similar
p16.h3: Overseas plants (Mexico and others) supplied to local voltage specs
p16.band: On a synchronized line, one stop is every stop — protect the line as a whole
p17.risk: Electrode coating and slitting are continuous processes: the moment they stop, the whole roll becomes scrap. And when utilities such as plating, boilers or compressors go down, the line takes even longer to resume.
p17.h1: Process tools and utilities (compressors, pumps, boilers) protected together
p17.h2: European sites use three-phase 400V, CE-certified models
p17.h3: Annual on-site inspection verifies the condition of every unit
p17.case: Case — Volta Energy Solutions (Hungary, EV battery modules)
p17.c3: Line stoppages · 53 units PASS at inspection
p17.band: 53 units in Hungary · all 41 sags compensated in 2023 · zero line stops

p18.d4: Rides and safety systems kept running without interruption

p18.w2: A ride that stops mid-course can require a rescue operation
p18.w3: Distributed equipment — too many units and too much capacity for a UPS
p18.h1: Small distributed units at each equipment control panel
p18.h2: No batteries or fans, so maintenance burden on public facilities stays minimal
p18.h3: Event logging integrated with the operator's control room
p18.band: When equipment carries people, a stop is a safety incident — sag protection for public infrastructure
